svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: how a cell makes and secretes a protein
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A gene in the nucleus is transcribed into mRNA, which leaves through a nuclear pore."], [3, "Ribosomes on the rough ER translate the mRNA. The protein enters the space inside the rough ER."], [5.5, "A transport vesicle buds off the rough ER and carries the protein to the Golgi apparatus."], [8, "The Golgi apparatus modifies the protein (for example adding carbohydrate) and packages it into a secretory vesicle."], [10.5, "The secretory vesicle moves to the cell surface membrane and fuses with it (exocytosis), releasing the protein, for example an enzyme or hormone."]]
svg.title: Animal cell as seen with an electron microscope
svg.desc: A generalised animal cell showing the cell surface membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus with nuclear envelope, pores and nucleolus, rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, ribosomes, lysosomes, centrioles and vesicles.
svg.text: A generalised cell: real cells are specialised and have more of some organelles. Not to scale.

g.data-info: Jelly-like fluid where many chemical reactions (metabolism) happen; contains the organelles.
Phospholipid bilayer with proteins: controls what enters and leaves the cell (partially permeable).
Contains the chromosomes (DNA), which control the cell’s activities by coding for proteins.
Double membrane around the nucleus, with nuclear pores that let mRNA out to the cytoplasm.
Dense region of the nucleus where ribosomes are made.
Flattened membrane sacs covered in ribosomes: makes proteins (especially for secretion) and transports them inside its sacs.
Very small organelles (no membrane) where proteins are made (translation). Free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough ER.
Membrane tubes without ribosomes: makes lipids and steroids.
Stack of flattened sacs: modifies proteins (e.g. adds carbohydrate) and packages them into vesicles for secretion or for use in the cell.
Site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy (as ATP). Double membrane; the inner one is folded into cristae.
Vesicles containing digestive enzymes that break down worn-out organelles and engulfed material.
A pair of small cylinders of microtubules at right angles; involved in forming the spindle in cell division (animal cells only).
Small membrane sacs that carry substances around the cell, for example from the ER to the Golgi and from the Golgi to the membrane.

g.text: 1 mRNA leaves the nucleus through a pore
2 Ribosomes on the rough ER make the protein
3 A vesicle carries it to the Golgi apparatus
4 The Golgi modifies and packages it
